Question: A speaker talked for sixty minutes to a full auditorium. Twenty percent of the audience heard the entire talk and ten percent slept through the entire talk. Half of the remainder heard one third of the talk and the other half heard two thirds of the talk. What was the average number of minutes of the talk heard by members of the audience?
Solution:
After accounting for the \(20\%\) who heard everything and the \(10\%\) who heard nothing, \(70\%\) remain. Half of this remainder is \(35\%\) of the whole audience. Thus \(35\%\) heard \(60/3=20\) minutes, and another \(35\%\) heard \(2(60)/3=40\) minutes.

The average is total listening minutes divided by the number of audience members. Each group's contribution is therefore its fraction of the audience multiplied by its listening time:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average}&=0.20(60)+0.10(0)\\
&\quad+0.35(20)+0.35(40)\\
&=12+0+7+14=33.
\end{aligned}
\]
The average is \(33\) minutes, choice D.
